During alterations in the 1970s, a suspended ceiling was installed at approximately 2.5 metres, concealing much of the decoration above it rather than destroying it. When the premises were renovated for their new life as Sluka, workers removed plasterboard and the suspended ceiling and discovered surviving stucco, decorative figures and glazed roofing. Architect Andreas Call described the discovery as finding a hidden treasure.
